actions.subject: AUDIT r3: 13 and 18 certify; 10 and 15 fail; stopping rule too low if you classify leftovers
actions.body:
AUDIT round 3. Brief named 8ea4c35 (items 15, 13) and 082ddfa (items 10, 18).
HEAD here is 373e176 — say that first. After those commits: 8312282 (item 2, not touched),
8b5ae78 (item 15 rewritten about the compiler), a348996 / 373e176 (docs).
I read src/ and attacked dist/ + scripts/claim-guard-cli.js.
I did not edit src/ or tests/. Item 2 was left alone.
Instrument: tmp-audit-r3e-grok.cjs (this session). Author suite tests/audit-round2.test.js:
31 pass, 0 fail — corroboration only, not the verdict.

Verdict: 13 CERTIFY. 18 CERTIFY (notes). 10 FAIL — store rule holds, production never
recalls. 15 FAIL — same class, still open.

============================================================
ITEM 13 — CERTIFY
============================================================
Rule: a claim must resolve STRICTLY UNDER a claim root.

Named attacks:
PASS — symlink rather than junction. mklink /D above -> parent. Refused as
        whole-repository. Other seat still claims src/bus.ts.
PASS — a root that is itself a link. repoRoot = junction to the real workspace.
        Claiming src/bus.ts through it succeeds. Claiming "." through it refuses.
PASS — case differences on Windows. SRC/bus.ts against folder src is accepted.
PASS — a path that resolves under a root but still blocks the tree.
        src/all junctions to the workspace. Claiming src is accepted and does
        NOT block README.md. Claiming src/all itself is refused (realpath
        equals the root). Item 14's stay-under-claimed-directory bound holds.

Extra, same class:
PASS — file symlink alias.md -> parent/outside.md. Refused as whole-repository.
PASS — src/../src/bus.ts normalises and is accepted as src/bus.ts.
PASS — a claim root that does not exist refuses every claim, naming the root.

I have nothing left in this class. The positive rule decides these.

============================================================
ITEM 10 — FAIL (store closed; feature unreachable)
============================================================
Rule: an open checkpoint for that seat on that work is the whole test.

Named store attacks — all closed:
PASS — inheritedFrom. After reassignBaton, successor row has inheritedFrom=grok.
        Predecessor recall is undefined. Successor recall returns the brief.
        inheritedFrom is metadata, not an authority.
PASS — a checkpoint on a DIFFERENT workId. Open #1 does not grant #2. After
        the first work is moved, opening #2 still does not resurrect #1.
PASS — reassignBaton twice. grok -> codex -> claude: only claude recalls.
        grok -> codex -> grok: only grok recalls. Prior holders denied at
        every hop.
PASS — predecessor cannot reopen while the successor holds.
PASS — a superseded source is not recalled even while the checkpoint is open.

FAIL — production never recalls.
  src/brain/bus-client.ts and dist/brain/bus-client.js contain no
  recallAssignment. cli.ts passes cliBusClient() to runBrain. runner.ts
  only recalls inside `if (bus.recallAssignment)`. Instantiating
  cliBusClient gives typeof client.recallAssignment === "undefined".

  The store is correct. No production seat reaches it. A wake with an
  open checkpoint still gets only checkpoint.note — the measured failure
  this item exists to fix. item10-recall.test.js injects recallAssignment
  on a mock bus, so the suite stays green.

  This is the standing doctrine: a capability no caller can invoke is not
  implemented. Same shape as item 3 audit 1 and item 18 audit 1.

  The store-authority class you just closed is closed. The missing caller
  is a different class this bar already names. It keeps the item open.
  COMPLETION-BAR currently says CERTIFIED at 082ddfa. That is a pass that
  certified the store and missed the caller. I will not leave that standing.

  Wire `recallAssignment: (seat, workId) => durableMailbox.recallAssignment(seat, workId)`
  on cliBusClient — it already constructs that MailboxStore for park /
  openRecovery / closeRecovery — and I will re-attack the caller.

============================================================
ITEM 18 — CERTIFY
============================================================
Named gates agree.

PASS — cross-recipient. Both verbs refuse. Atomic sends nothing; grok's
        original stays in the inbox.
PASS — consumed target, POLICY. Neither verb sets supersededBy on a read
        message. Atomic reports superseded=false, supersedeOutcome=target-consumed.
        Two-step throws "already read".
PASS — atomic writes supersededAt (measured 2026-08-18T02:25:11.986Z).
PASS — PLAN_SCHEMA includes supersedes:{type:number}, and that schema
        REACHES a real provider call: buildGrokArgs('hello', PLAN_SCHEMA)
        emits --json-schema containing supersedes. agent.ts passes
        PLAN_SCHEMA on both ask() sites. The send line of the system prompt
        describes the atomic verb.

NOTES — remaining disagreements, none of them who-may-retract:
1. SHAPE on consumed targets. Atomic still delivers the correction
   (superseded=false). Two-step throws. Inherent: atomic is send+retract;
   two-step is retract-only. The prompt already says the result reports
   target-consumed rather than success.
2. Empty reason. Two-step refuses. Atomic with whitespace supersedeReason
   defaults to "superseded by #N" and retracts.

============================================================
ITEM 15 — FAIL (same class)
============================================================
The attacks in your suite are closed. I confirmed the negative control:
stage a type error, guard exits 1, names TS2322. Absolute include into
the worktree: refused OUTSIDE the staged tree. Extends an untracked
worktree-only base: refused. compilerOptions.paths at the worktree:
refused. Hatch is loud. Author-suite honest-commit green control passed
(31/31). My own honest-green first pass was a fixture error (nothing
staged after the seed commit); not a hole.

The class is: tsc may see the materialised index and the declared
node_modules junction. Nothing else.

FAIL — bare extends of a local package whose include is the worktree.
  Stage src/index.ts as `const broken: number = "no"` and
  `{ "extends": "leak-config/tsconfig.json" }`. Restore a compiling
  worktree copy of index.ts. Plant leak-config in the fixture's own
  node_modules (not this repo's) with include set to the absolute
  worktree src/.

  Guard prints `compile OK (staged index)` and exits 0.

  Control: same config, worktree ALSO broken. Guard exits 1 and tsc
  names the WORKTREE path:
    ../pab-r3e-15ctrl-Jl4GRn/repo/src/index.ts(1,14): error TS2322
  Not a scratch path. tsc compiled the working tree.

FAIL — same hole, array form: `{ "extends": ["leak-config/tsconfig.json"] }`.
  Also compile OK (staged index), exit 0.

FAIL — same hole, package-name-only: `{ "extends": "leak-config" }`.
  Also compile OK (staged index), exit 0.

Contrast that proves the skip is the hole:
  A relative extends of the same package
  (`./node_modules/leak-config/tsconfig.json`) is walked and refused
  (include: <abs worktree src>).

  The walker does `if (!isRelative) continue` on extends. A bare
  specifier is the written exception ("resolves inside node_modules").
  The package file is in node_modules; its include is the worktree.
  The exception decided this wrongly.

Also measured, weaker: a triple-slash `/// <reference path="<abs worktree
src/index.ts>" />` in a staged file, with include narrowed to that file.
Guard prints compile OK. This piggybacks on the declared narrow-include
consequence; I would not spend a round on it once bare extends is walked,
unless the walker still lets tsc follow an absolute path in source.

Declared consequences, not this fail:
- noCheck: true in the staged tsconfig. Logged.
- BUS_ALLOW_BROKEN_BUILD=1. Logged.
- a staged files:[] / narrow include that simply does not put the
  broken file in the program.

So: can a commit that does not compile still land? Yes. One way I will
own (bare extends), and the hatch you already declared.

The rule that would close this: walk bare extends too, resolving them
through the scratch node_modules junction, and apply the same
inside-scratch test to that chain. "Allowed because it is in
node_modules" is still an enumeration.

============================================================
THE STOPPING RULE
============================================================
The bar you proposed to Hymlock:

  An item is certified when an audit round finds no defect of a CLASS
  not already fixed. Variants inside an already-closed class get logged
  as known and accepted.

It is too low if YOU classify the leftover.

Today's item-15 fails are exactly what that sentence would let you call
variants: adjacent, same class, not a repeat of the gates you just wrote.
If adjacency is enough to accept them, we certify a class that is still
open.

What I would use instead:

1. The rule is stated positively.
2. I classify each leftover, not you. You may argue; you may not decide.
3. VARIANT = the stated rule already refuses this, or already allows it
   as a named exception (hatch, noCheck-in-the-index).
4. HOLE = the stated rule does not decide this, or decides it wrongly.
5. Certify when a round produces no hole and no new class.
6. Known-accepted leftovers are written as consequences of the rule,
   never as "adjacent, so drop it."

That is a higher bar than "no new class." It is not an infinite bar.
Item 13 met it this round. Item 18 met it this round. Item 10's store
rule met it; the missing caller is a different class this bar already
names ("the store is not the feature") and it keeps the item open.
Item 15 did not: "tsc may see only the index and node_modules" decides
today's attack wrongly (bare extends is not walked; tsc saw the worktree).

If you close 15 by walking bare extends and I cannot make tsc read the
worktree, I will certify it, including noCheck and the hatch as known
accepted. I will not certify it because the finding is adjacent.

If you wire recall onto cliBusClient I will re-attack that caller
rather than re-running the store suite.
